name: Heat-killed (tyndallised) Lactobacillus
short: Infants with eczema given heat-inactivated L. GG formula: gut symptoms, diarrhoea; pilot stopped (35 infants). Children, other heat-killed strains: few events. Colic product: no adverse-event data.
text: The colic product (chamomile and lemon balm with tyndallised, heat-killed Lactobacillus acidophilus, taken together): its trial abstract does not report adverse events, and no source gives adverse-event data for this exact product. Infants (a different strain; the abstract does not name its species): in a randomised, double-blind pilot in 35 infants with eczema and cow's milk allergy (mean age 5.5 months), formula with heat-inactivated Lactobacillus GG was associated with adverse gut symptoms and diarrhoea, and recruitment was stopped after the pilot phase. Children (other heat-killed products by mouth): in a placebo-controlled trial in 80 children aged 3 months to 4 years with acute diarrhoea, Lactobacillus LB was well tolerated, with one child having an adverse effect (that abstract does not name the species or say directly that the bacteria were killed; a systematic review of trials in children under 5, and the title of another trial, describe Lactobacillus LB as heat-killed Lactobacillus acidophilus); in a placebo-controlled trial in children aged 1 to 12 with moderate eczema, tyndallised Lactobacillus rhamnosus showed no significant differences in safety parameters (100 children assessed); and in an open study of 98 children aged 5 to 15, lozenges of heat-killed Lactobacillus helveticus were reported to have no adverse effects. Adults: in a placebo-controlled trial in 100 healthy adults, heat-killed Lactobacillus acidophilus for 12 weeks gave safety outcomes comparable with placebo, with no serious adverse events. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
